subject: Ephemeral session data, ownership of prompts/responses & subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@holohealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@holohealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on session handling, ownership & subprocessors (HoloHealth)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Before procurement can move forward we need to lock down a few items in the DPA and operational runbook. Legal looped me in. High level asks:

1) No-training/no-derivative commitment: your standard DPA language states a model-improvement opt-out, but we need an explicit operational guarantee that HoloHealth data will not be used for model training or persistent parameter updates. Is that an SLA-able commitment or an appendix we sign?

2) Prompt/response ownership: For ephemeral conversational sessions (chat flows), can we get a statement that HoloHealth retains ownership of prompts/responses and that Redwood will not assert derivative IP claims on tenant outputs? We need language we can hand to product counsel.

3) Ephemeral session handling / retention: Our security team requires that session transcripts can be configured to auto-delete after configurable TTL (30/90/365 days). Can you describe how Redwood handles ephemeral KV/prefix caching and what controls we’d have to ensure deletion and non-persistence to training stores?

4) Subprocessor gating and cross-border transfer: We need a subprocessor gating workflow (review/approval window for new subprocessors) and confirmation of onshore options for EU/US processing for the tenant. Also a current inventory export (CSV) would be helpful.

If you can share an operational evidence pack (how deletion is implemented, attestation, subprocessor inventory), we’ll pass to our procurement and legal teams.

Appreciate a short note of next steps and any DocuSign links you expect in the procurement phase.

Best,
Michael
Michael Sanders
Head of Cloud Integrations — HoloHealth
attach: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@holohealth.com>
Cc: legal@holohealth.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on session handling, ownership & subprocessors (HoloHealth)

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list. Looping in ops and privacy so we can provide concrete artifacts. Short answers up front:

- No-training/no-derivative: Yes — we offer a binding DPA appendix that includes a no-training commitment per-tenant. It is operationally enforced by a tenant-level flag (no_model_improve = true) that disables logging to training pipelines and blocks any parameter updates; we can include the appendix language for your counsel.

- Ownership: We will include contract language confirming HoloHealth retains ownership of prompts/responses and that Redwood grants only the processing rights necessary to serve the tenant.

- Ephemeral retention: We support configurable TTL on session transcripts. When TTL is reached we perform a secure deletion flow (KV cache purge + metadata tombstones + S3 lifecycle delete) and an attestation record is logged to the audit store.

- Subprocessor gating & inventory: Attaching the current subprocessor inventory and a short evidence pack. For new subprocessors we can offer a 30-day review window and an escalation path to your security contact. Onshore routing options are available for US/EU tenants (VPC/private deployment + dedicated capacity).

Next steps:
1) I’ll send an internal operational note (below) to the product/ops team asking for the artifact links and deletion proof.
2) Priyom — can you draft the appendix language and attach the no-training attestation artifact?
3) Michael/legal — if you can indicate which retention TTL you prefer (30/90/365) we’ll prototype the tenant flag and provide the attestation.

Sharing the following attachments now: no_train_evidence_package_v1.zip; subprocessor_inventory_2028Q3.csv; ephemeral-session-retention-diagram.png

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of GTM Privacy & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
attach: no_train_evidence_package_v1.zip (zip), subprocessor_inventory_2028Q3.csv (csv), ephemeral-session-retention-diagram.png (png)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: HoloHealth ask — evidence & appendix draft (action items)

Team —

HoloHealth (prospect in procurement) needs operational evidence for a no-training/no-derivative commitment plus subprocessor gating and TTL controls. Procurement wants this in the next week. Action items:

- Priyom: please draft a DPA appendix with explicit tenant-level no-training clause and proposed indemnity/assurance language. Include a short 2-paragraph operational description of the tenant flag enforcement and how we prevent data from reaching training pipelines.

- Neha: export the subprocessor inventory (CSV attached in reply) and add a row-level field indicating which subprocessors are used for ephemeral session handling vs metric telemetry. Also outline the 30-day gating workflow steps we would commit to.

- David: can ops produce a short attestation (~1 paragraph) describing the deletion pipeline (KV purge, S3 lifecycle, audit tombstone) and whether deletion is irreversible within our primary storage tier? Also confirm whether we can offer an onshore-only processing option for this account until the DPA is signed.

- Kimberly: I’ll own communicating the artifacts to Michael and coordinating any minor redline cycles with legal. We should surface estimated lead time for dedicated routing and any costs associated.

Target timeline: artifacts + draft appendix by Fri 2028-10-05 EOD.

Thanks —
Kim

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: HoloHealth ask — evidence & appendix draft (action items)

Kim — attaching the draft appendix and an operational note. Highlights:

- Draft appendix: tenant-level "No Model Improvement" clause that is contractually binding. Language includes: (i) definition of "Customer Data" and "Derived Outputs"; (ii) explicit prohibition on using Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or update models; (iii) audit rights to confirm the tenant flag state; (iv) remedy language in case of breach.

- Evidence pack (summary): we will provide the following artifacts:
  * runbook: no_train_enforcement_v1.md (explains the tenant flag and how training pipelines are gated)
  * attestation: deletion_attestation_hl_v1.pdf (signed by Head of Ops)
  * subprocessor CSV (already attached to external reply)
  * retention diagram (ephemeral-session-retention-diagram.png)

- Technical note on TTL: the tenant TTL configuration controls both ephemeral KV cache retention and long-term transcript persistence. When TTL expires we trigger an event that (a) invalidates session keys, (b) issues a purge job that wipes objects in primary store, and (c) emits an audit tombstone. The purge job is irreversible for primary objects; backups are on a 30-day retention cycle (we can shorten for onshore/dedicated tenants as a contractual option).

Attachments in this email (stubs): no_train_appendix_draft.docx, runbook_no_train_enforcement_v1.md, deletion_attestation_hl_v1.pdf

Flagging cost items: dedicated onshore routing and shortened backup retention will have additional monthly costs. I included placeholder numbers in the draft appendix.

Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
attach: no_train_appendix_draft.docx (docx), runbook_no_train_enforcement_v1.md (text), deletion_attestation_hl_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — that was fast and very helpful. Legal will review the appendix and the attestation. A few quick follow-ups:

- TTL: we want the default proof path to be 90 days, but we need the ability to set 30 days for pilot accounts. Please confirm that shortening backup retention to 7 days for the pilot is something you can commit to for the duration of the pilot.

- Audit rights: legal will want to confirm that the audit tombstone includes a verifiable hash/timestamp for deletions and that we can request a one-time export of audit records.

- Procurement: procurement asked whether you have a standard order form/DocuSign template for the appendix and whether the deal team can get an initial quote for dedicated onshore routing + reduced backup retention. If you can send the DocuSign link and a ballpark quote we can move to procurement review next week.

Looking forward to the draft appendix.

Best,
Michael
